main_text.p: ut qui folus eft Confcientiæ Dominus & fupremus Legiflator; qui eam homini indidit; qui ejus folus cognitor eft & judex; qui folus poteftatem habet animam, prout legem ipfius fervaverit aut violaverit, fervandi & perdendi, juxta illud, Jac. 4, 12.

p.i: 12. Unus eft Legiflator qui poteft fervare & perdere.

main_text.p: Id quod apud omnes, quotquot ufpiam funt hominum, adeò in confeffo eft, ut non facilè reperiatur, qui id ipfum in thefi non ultrò largiatur esse veriffimum. Aft in hypothefi, ubi quid agendum eft, nescio quâ cordis humani pravitate fieri folet, ut plerique mortalium (etiam eorum, qui nec sibi videntur, nec aliis, omnem prorfus confcientiæ curam abjecisse,) tàm pronis affectibus ad ea fe rantur quæ facta cupiunt, ut ea non ad unicam fupremam regulam fideliter exigenda adducant, (quæ tamen sola poteft fecuram præstare confcientiam ;) fed fatis esse ducant ad Confcientiæ suæ securitatem, si aut bonæ intentionis prætextu, aut javeti viri exemplo, aut alicujus magni nominis Theologi authoritate se factâque sua quoquo modo tueri potuerint. Quæ cordis humani deceptio, quum & omnibus seculis nimium invaluerit, & noviffimis hisce temporibus vel maximè; rem utiliffimam me facturam judicavi, & his quibus nunc vivitur moribus pernecessariam, si tres iftas vulgatiffimas ἀγνωσίας, à quibus tot conscientiis periculosiffimè illuditur, de medio sublatum irem. Eft ergo an oftendendum, quàm ad indagandam veram propriam Confcientiæ regulam defcendatur, non e in re aliquâ faciendâ ad Confcientiæ securitatem tis prasfidii, si id quod fit aut bonâ intentione si aut viri alicujus nitatur vel pii exemplo, vel de judicio. De reliquis duabus (si Deus concesser posthac videbitur: de eâ quæ primo loco occurrit Bonâ sc. Intentione nunc agendum.

page.notes: The Greek word after "tres iftas vulgatiffimas" is smudged; I could not read it letter by letter: [illegible, ~7 letters] would be the honest reading, but I have left the best guess above, so please check that word. The bottom-right "IV." is read as a gathering signature and "Ubi" as the catchword; both are uncertain. The right edge of the scan shows the adjacent page's text (IV, and fragments such as "ftem", "dico", "Intent"), which is excluded. Some words at the right edge of the text column are blurred by the gutter shadow (e.g. "vivit", "fallendum") and were read with reasonable confidence but may need checking. "fi" is the printed long-s form and was written as "si". The line "12. Unus est..." was taken as a numbered thesis in italics and set as its own paragraph.
